A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same EOGS study, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v1 includes Appendices A–B, whereas v2 ends with references despite citing supplementary results and implementation details. That unavailable supplement limits the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EOGS reconstruction results on seven satellite scenes, component ablations, parameter and visibility studies, and qualitative appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original reconstruction experiments and analyses, with additional S2P comparison results and ablation training times.

M1.justification: The affine-camera model, shadow mapping, color corrections, regularizers and optimization procedure remain unchanged. Equations (1)–(21) match; the added references and supplementary cross-references do not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: Both evaluate satellite photogrammetry on the same four JAX and three IARPA scenes, including whole-area, foliage-masked and visibility-based evaluations. Omission of supplementary visualizations does not remove the scene coverage retained in Table 1.

E2.justification: v2 adds S2P to the unmasked comparison in Table 1. EO-NeRF, SAT-NGP and Sat-Mesh remain, and the foliage-masked comparator set is unchanged. S2P was previously discussed but had no reported comparison row.

E3.justification: The stated elevation-MAE and training-time metrics, foliage masking, optimization schedule and ablation configurations are retained. Exact view counts are newly disclosed; the additional timing entries do not establish changed experimental procedures or reruns.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds direct timing evidence for the sparsity ablation: 4.27 minutes without sparsity versus 2.85 minutes for full EOGS. The existing accuracy, parameter and visibility analyses remain. v1's supplementary albedo/shadow comparisons are absent from the supplied v2.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Averaging and the linear-regression analysis of component effects remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All existing table values and plotted trends are retained. v2 adds S2P results, including JAX/IARPA mean MAEs of 1.53/1.78 m and 20-minute training, plus Table 2 timings of 4.18, 4.27 and 2.85 minutes. Additional qualitative results from v1's appendices are absent from the supplied v2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, affine-camera and directional-light assumptions, rendering derivations and loss formulations are unchanged. No new theorem, proof or mathematical correction appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims remain: EOGS adapts Gaussian splatting to satellite photogrammetry with approximately EO-NeRF accuracy and roughly 300-fold faster training. Combining the three regularizer contribution bullets preserves their scientific meaning.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of shadow modeling and regularization, qualifications concerning foliage and low image coverage, and suggested remedies through additional regularization or improved initialization.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link, exact per-scene view counts in Table 1 and a GENCI-IDRIS computing-resource acknowledgement. Newly referenced sun-camera, Gaussian-count and memory details are not actually included in the supplied PDF.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven references while retaining the earlier bibliography. It explicitly credits the previously cited 3DGSMCMC as inspiration for opacity regularization and adds Mip-NeRF 360 and LOLNeRF when acknowledging prior work on hard surfaces.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, compacts the author block and contribution list, adds acknowledgements and cross-references, and makes small language edits. Most prose and the main section order remain unchanged; the appendix sections are absent.

P2.justification: The supplied v2 omits the extensive appendix displays in Figures 8–18, although the duplicated JAX 214 example remains in Figure 5. It also expands both tables, relocates and shrinks Figure 7, and lowers the resolution of Figure 5's zoom panels. The visual presentation is substantially reduced.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens comparison through S2P, directly supports sparsity's efficiency benefit with timings, and improves attribution. However, it omits v1's extensive supplementary visual evidence and points to an unavailable supplement for additional results and technical details. These gains and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment from the supplied PDFs.
